title: P300 dataset BI2015a from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
description: EEG recordings from 43 healthy participants playing Brain Invaders, a visual P300 brain-computer interface game based on an oddball paradigm with a grid of 36 symbols. The study examined how flash duration (50, 80 or 110 ms) affects a calibration-less P300 BCI that uses wet electrodes and an adaptive Riemannian classifier. Data were recorded with 32 channels at 512 Hz over three game sessions per subject, with resting-state and eyes-closed recordings before and after.
methods_description: 32 active wet electrodes (g.USBamp, g.tec; 10-10 montage) recorded at 512 Hz with the reference on the right earlobe and ground at Fz. Stimulation and acquisition ran in OpenViBE with USB-synchronized tagging. Each participant played three game sessions of nine levels, one session per flash duration. A real-time adaptive Riemannian Minimum Distance to Mean classifier provided calibration-free online feedback. About one minute of resting state and eyes-closed EEG was recorded before and after the sessions.
